note: Strong derived-substance markers APPROVED by the owner (2026-11-21): whey powder and whey solids. CLASSIFICATION-BEARING: a list holding one is Group 4 (FAO p.10: 'The presence in the list of ingredients of one or more of these food substances identifies a product as ultra-processed'). Three admissible sources name whey: FAO p.9 ('whey protein'), Monteiro et al. 2018 PHN 21(1):5-17 (PMC10261019; names whey among substances directly extracted from foods; licence unverified, paraphrase) and Martinez Steele et al. 2022 (PMC10127522; whey among non-culinary substances; licence unverified, paraphrase).

clause.where: FAO 2019 (Monteiro et al.), ca5644en.pdf, p. 9 (section 2, ingredients characteristic of ultra-processed foods)
clause.text: include varieties of sugars (fructose, high-fructose corn syrup, ‘fruit juice concentrates’, invert sugar, maltodextrin, dextrose, lactose), modified oils (hydrogenated or interesterified oils) and sources of protein (hydrolysed proteins, soya protein isolate, gluten, casein, whey protein, and ‘mechanically separated meat’)

basis.where: FAO 2019, ca5644en.pdf, p. 10 (section 3, identifying ultra-processed foods)
basis.text: The presence in the list of ingredients of one or more of these food substances identifies a product as ultra-processed.
